takeaways: Every page or screen has a title that describes its topic or purpose.
On the web, it is the title shown in the browser tab and read first by screen readers. In apps, it is each screen’s title.
Good titles are unique and put the specific part first, such as “Order 4821 – Orders – Shopname”, so people can tell tabs and pages apart.
Designers write the titles, including for single-page apps, dialogs that act as steps, and errors, and hand them to developers.
failures: Every page titled with just the company name
A single-page app whose title never changes
Checkout steps that all share the title “Checkout”
check: List every page or screen in the flow and write its title next to the frame.
Read the titles alone, in a list, and check each one tells you where you are.
In the build, check the browser tab or screen title changes as you move through the flow.

quiz.question: A three-step checkout keeps the same browser tab title on every step. Which titles would you specify?
options: “Delivery – Step 1 of 3 – Checkout – Shopname”, and so on for each step
“Shopname” on every step, for brand consistency
“Checkout” on every step, with the step shown in the page heading
quiz.why: A title that changes with each step tells screen reader users where they landed and helps everyone tell tabs apart. Putting the step first means it is not cut off in a narrow tab.

spec: Write the title for every page and screen, including empty, error and success states.
Use one pattern across the product, such as “Page – Section – Product”.
For single-page apps and step flows, note when the title changes.
review: If this tab were one of twenty open, could you find it?
Does the title change when the content changes?
Does the title match the main heading on the page?
tradeoff: Marketing often wants the brand name first. Put the page first and the brand last: the brand is still there, and people can tell pages apart.
system: Give every page template a required title field and a shared title pattern, so no screen ships untitled.
pitch: The page title is the first thing a screen reader says and the only thing people see in a crowded tab bar. It should tell them where they are.
